545	## 2. Match rules
546	
547	### IPv4
548	- Octet: 1–3 digits, value 0–255, leading zeros allowed (`010`, `001`, `00` all fine; `0004` rejected). Equivalent: `25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9]?[0-9]`.
549	- Exactly 4 octets. 3 or 5+ octet runs: no dedicated match — but `0.1.2.3.4` matches the FIRST four octets (`0.1.2.3`), leaving `.4` plain (leftmost wins; a following `.` does not block).
550	- Boundary: ASCII word chars `[A-Za-z0-9_]` on either side block the match (`v1.2.3.4`, `x10.0.0.1`, `10.0.0.1x`, `10.0.0.1_`, `1.2.3.456` all rejected entirely). Non-ASCII word chars do NOT block (`é10.0.0.1` and `10.0.0.1é` match) → ASCII `\b` semantics. `-`, `=`, `,`, `[`, `:`, `.`, whitespace are fine neighbors (`1.2.3.4:8080` → IP styled, `:8080` plain).
551	- Leftmost-greedy: `999.1.1.1` → no match at all (can't slide into `99.1.1.1` because the preceding `9` blocks).
552	
553	### IPv4 CIDR
554	- `IP/mask` where mask = 1–2 digits, value 0–32, leading zeros allowed (`/0`, `/00`, `/03`, `/24`, `/32` styled; `/` red, mask italic-blue).
555	- Invalid mask (`/33`–`/99`, i.e. 1–2 digits + ASCII word boundary, value >32): **the whole token is left completely unstyled** — the bare IP does NOT fall back (see §4 non-determinism).
556	- 3+ digit masks (`/128`, `/024`, `/033`, `/003`): CIDR rejected, bare IP IS highlighted, mask left plain.
557	- Mask followed by letter/underscore (`/24x`, `/2x`, `/33x`, `/24_`): bare IP highlighted, `/24x` plain.
558	- Mask followed by punctuation works: `/24-` → `/24` styled, `-` plain.
559	- `1.2.3.4/` and `1.2.3.4/x` → bare IP styled, rest plain.
560	- Behavioral regex equivalent: `\b(oct\.){3}oct(?:/(3[0-2]|[0-2]?[0-9]))?\b(?!/[0-9]{1,2}\b)` with ASCII `\b`.
561	
562	### IPv6

655	# tailspin 5.6.0 — JSON highlighter: behavioral spec
656	
657	## 0. Activation model (crucial)
658	
659	- Processing is **line-based**. The JSON highlighter fires **only if the entire line** (after trimming leading/trailing JSON whitespace: space, tab, `\r`, `\n`) **parses as one complete, strict JSON value**. Anything before/after (log prefix, trailing text, second JSON value) disables it entirely:
660	  - `2022-09-09 INFO {"msg": "hi"}` → line passed through untouched.
661	  - `{"a":1} {"b":2}`, `{"a":1}{"b":2}`, `[1,2] extra` → untouched.
662	  - `  {"a":1}  ` → accepted; surrounding whitespace is **consumed** (output starts at `{`).
663	- Any JSON value type qualifies: object, array, string, number, boolean, null. Bare `4e2` → output `400.0`; bare ` 42  ` → `42`; `"just a string"` → highlighted.
664	- Strictness is serde_json-like: single quotes, unquoted keys, trailing commas, `undefined`, `007`, `1e400` (out of f64 range), lone surrogates (`"\ud83d"`), raw control bytes inside strings → all rejected, line passed through verbatim.
665	- **Recursion limit: 128.** 127 nested arrays highlight; 128 do not (line passed through unchanged).
666	- Empty line → empty line; whitespace-only line → unchanged.
667	
668	## 1. Parse → re-serialize → highlight
669	
670	The line is **parsed into a value and re-emitted in a canonical format**; highlighting is applied to the *re-serialized* text (proved: `{"n": 4e2}` with all groups on → the numbers group colors `400.0`, not `4e2`).
671	
672	Serialization format (single line):
673	- Objects: `{ "k": v, "k2": v2 }` — space after `{`, space before `}`, `": "` after key, `", "` between entries. Empty object → `{ }`.
674	- Arrays: `[1, 2]` — **no** padding inside brackets, `", "` separator. Empty array → `[]`.
675	- Key order = first-insertion order; **duplicate keys: last value wins, first position kept** (`{"b":1,"a":2,"b":3}` → `{ "b": 3, "a": 2 }`) — IndexMap/`preserve_order` semantics.
676	- Numbers: integers within i64/u64 range stay exact (`18446744073709551615`, `-9223372036854775808`); outside range they become floats (`18446744073709551616` → `1.8446744073709552e19`). Floats use ryu-style shortest form: `1e10`→`10000000000.0`, `1.50`→`1.5`, `-0.0`→`-0.0`, `1e-7`→`1e-7`, `1.0e+22`→`1e22`, `5e-324`→`5e-324`.
677	- Strings are **fully escape-decoded and re-emitted raw, with no re-escaping**: `\u00e9`→`é`, `\t`→literal tab, `\n`→**literal newline byte in the output line**, `\/`→`/`, `\"`→raw `"`, `\\`→raw `\`, `\u001b`→raw ESC (so decoded output can be invalid JSON / contain escape bytes). Same for keys (`{"k\u00e9y":1}` → key `kéy`).
678	
679	## 2. Exact styling (default theme)
680	
681	Every styled segment is `\x1b[2m` + content + `\x1b[0m` (faint/dim). Six style slots, **all default to faint**:
682	
683	| slot (theme array index) | element |
684	|---|---|
685	| 0 | object key text (inside the quotes) |
686	| 1 | all double-quote characters (key quotes AND string-value quotes) |
687	| 2 | `{` `}` |
688	| 3 | `[` `]` |
689	| 4 | `,` |
690	| 5 | `:` |
691	
692	**Unstyled (emitted plain):** string-value content, numbers, `true`/`false`/`null`, and the single-space separators after `{`, before `}`, and after `:`/`,` (spaces belong to no styled segment).
693	
694	Canonical example — input `{"key": "value"}` (note the re-spacing):
695	
696	```
697	^[[2m{^[[0m ^[[2m"^[[0m^[[2mkey^[[0m^[[2m"^[[0m^[[2m:^[[0m ^[[2m"^[[0mvalue^[[2m"^[[0m ^[[2m}^[[0m
698	```
699	
700	i.e. `\x1b[2m{\x1b[0m \x1b[2m"\x1b[0m\x1b[2mkey\x1b[0m\x1b[2m"\x1b[0m\x1b[2m:\x1b[0m \x1b[2m"\x1b[0mvalue\x1b[2m"\x1b[0m \x1b[2m}\x1b[0m`
701	
702	Array example `[1, "two"]`: `^[[2m[^[[0m1^[[2m,^[[0m ^[[2m"^[[0mtwo^[[2m"^[[0m^[[2m]^[[0m` — note `,` and `]` can abut with no space (`"two"` then `,` then space).
703	
704	A missing input trailing newline is added; a present one is preserved.
705	
706	## 3. Theme configurability
707	
708	`theme.toml` accepts `json = [Style × 6]` (order = table above). Style struct supports at least `fg`, `bg`, `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `faint` (sequence emitted as attributes ascending then `bg` then `fg`: `^[[1;2;3;4;44;31m`). Unknown fields/sections are silently ignored; malformed TOML → `Error: × TOML parse error ...` on stderr, exit 1. An empty `{}` slot = no styling. Default = all six `{ faint = true }`.
709	
710	## 4. Interaction with other groups (default run, all enabled)
711	
712	Highlighting is span-based with **no overlap: once a span is styled, later groups can't restyle it**, and matches that would *span* styled boundaries fail. JSON runs first.
713	
714	- Keys are fully consumed by JSON dim → keywords, `--highlight` custom words, numbers never recolor keys (`{"INFO": 1}` key stays dim; `--highlight red:msg` doesn't touch key `"msg"`).
715	- String-value *content* is unstyled, so other groups apply inside values on the **re-serialized** text: severity keywords (`INFO`→`^[[37m…^[[0m`), numbers (`42`, `400.0`→`^[[36m`), dates (`2022-09-22T08:11:36.171800155Z` gets full date styling), urls (`http`→`^[[2;31m`, host→`^[[2;34m`, path→`^[[34m`), custom `--highlight` words (→`^[[31m` etc.).
716	- Quotes group is fully suppressed on JSON lines (its `"…"` matches need the quote chars, already dimmed by JSON).
717	- With `--disable json` on a pure JSON line, it is treated as plain text: quotes group colors all `"…"` yellow (`^[[33m`), numbers cyan, keywords apply; and a keyword hit *inside* quotes suppresses the quotes match for that string (e.g. `{"a": "INFO"}` → `{"a": "^[[37mINFO^[[0m"}` — quotes uncolored), showing builtin keywords run before quotes.
718	- `--enable json` disables all other regex groups (per man page: "`--enable` disables all highlighting groups except the ones specified") but **not** builtin keywords — `INFO happened` with `--enable json` still yields `^[[37mINFO^[[0m`. That's why `--enable json --disable-builtin-keywords` is the clean isolation combo.
719	
720	## 5. Surprises / quirks
721	
722	- **Re-serialization mutates content**: spacing normalized, numbers reformatted, escapes decoded raw (including raw newlines, tabs, ESC bytes into the output). 723	- Numbers/booleans/null are never dimmed by the JSON group — on bare-scalar lines the only visible effect is normalization; on `true`/`42` lines the output is indistinguishable from passthrough except whitespace trimming.
724	- The numbers-group regex apparently excludes a leading `-`: with all groups on, `{"n": -0}` → `-^[[36m0.0^[[0m` (minus left plain).
725	- Invalid UTF-8: if the **first** line contains invalid UTF-8 → hard fail `Error: × stream did not contain valid UTF-8`, exit 1, no output. Later lines with bad bytes are lossy-converted to U+FFFD and processing continues, exit 0.
726	- Exit code is 0 for all highlighting paths, including malformed JSON.
727	- Example logs: only `example1` (lines 113–117, pure-JSON log lines) triggers the JSON path; `example5` and others have no pure-JSON lines, so the group never activates there.</subagent>

894	## 6. `[[keywords]]` and `[[regexes]]` semantics
895	
896	- keywords: literal match (regex metachars escaped: `f.o`, `a+b`, `.*` match literally), case-sensitive (`FOO`≠`foo`), regex `\b` word boundaries (`foobar`, `afoo`, `a_foo`, `foo2` don't match; `foo-bar`, `(foo)`, `café foo` match; unicode letters count as word chars). 897	- regexes: raw regex, no implicit boundaries (`afoo` matches). **Capture-group rule: if the regex has exactly one capture group, only that group's text is styled; with zero or ≥2 groups the whole match is styled** (`f(o+)`→`oo`; `(f)o(o)`→`foo`; `a(x)c(y)e`→`axcye`; `(?:f)(o+)`→`oo`).
898	- **Precedence (high→low):** config `[[regexes]]` > builtin regex highlighters (numbers, dates, …) > builtin keywords > config `[[keywords]]` > CLI `--highlight`. Among equal-priority entries, **first entry wins**.

1136	# Behavioral Spec: General Input/Output Processing (tailspin v5.6.0)
1137	
1138	## 0. Three distinct I/O modes
1139	
1140	| Mode | Trigger | Pipeline |
1141	|---|---|---|
1142	| **stdin mode** | input from pipe or `<` redirect | direct print to stdout, streaming |
1143	| **file pager mode** | `FILE` arg, default | highlights into a **temp file** `/tmp/.tmpXXXXXX/tailspin.temp.<uuid>`, then runs the pager |
1144	| **file print mode** | `FILE` arg with `-p/--print` | direct print, but with different quirks (below) |
1145	
1146	- File mode **always** invokes the pager, even when stdout is a pipe and even for tiny files (verified with a logging pager shim). Stdin mode **never** pages when piped, even at 50k lines.
1147	- Default pager invocation: `less --ignore-case --RAW-CONTROL-CHARS -- <tempfile>` with env `LESSSECURE=1` added.
1148	- `--pager 'cmd [FILE]'` must contain the `[FILE]` placeholder; bare `--pager cat` fails: `Error:   × Could not parse custom pager command`, exit 1, no output. The pager error label is hardcoded as `less::non_zero_exit` even for custom pagers.
1149	- Only one `FILE` arg accepted; two args → clap error `unexpected argument`, exit 2. Invalid `--enable` value → clap error, exit 2.
1150	
1151	## 1. Trailing newline / empty / blank lines (stdin mode)
1152	
1153	- Input **with** final `\n`: output byte-identical structure, no extra newline.
1154	- Input **without** final `\n`: a `\n` is **appended**. `printf 'hello world'` → `hello world\n`. Even works after `\r`: `'a\rb'` → `a\rb\n`; `'\r'` → `\r\n`.
1155	- Empty stdin → empty output, exit 0.
1156	- `'\n'` → `'\n'`; `'\n\n\n'` → `'\n\n\n'`; trailing/interior blank lines preserved exactly (`'a\n\n'` → `'a\n\n'`).

1159	
1160	- **CRLF stripped**: file `'a\r\nb\r\n'` → `a\nb\n` (matches Rust `str::lines()` semantics: `\r` removed only as part of `\r\n`; lone mid-line `\r` and a trailing `\r` without `\n` are preserved: `'x\ry\n'` → `x\ry\n`; `'a\nb\r'` → `a\nb\r\n`). In **stdin mode `\r` is never stripped**: `'a\r\nb\r\n'` → `a\r\nb\r\n`.
1161	- **Pager mode, zero complete lines** (file has no `\n` at all, or is empty): output gets a **spurious leading `\n`**: file `'no newline at end'` → `'\nno newline at end\n'`; file `'x'` → `'\nx\n'`; **empty file → `'\n'`** (stdin empty → empty!). Files with ≥1 complete line behave normally (`'a\nb'` → `'a\nb\n'`).
1162	- **`-p` print mode: the final unterminated line is LOST**: `'a\nb'` → `'a\n'`; `'x'` → `'\n'`; `'a\rb'` → `'\n'`. (Empty file → `'\n'`.) This is a data-loss bug; pager mode is lossless.
1163	- Otherwise file vs stdin output is byte-identical for normal newline-terminated ASCII content.
